title: A fictional sales decision
question: Which client groups should receive extra sales effort over the next 90 days?
context: Fictional demonstration, with no commercial evidence supplied. Existing clients are active paying clients at the start of the period; new clients are everyone else. The split concerns extra effort above the already planned baseline, not products, channels or how much effort to allocate.
nextQuestion: What should the extra sales effort achieve within 90 days?

nodes.label: Allocate extra sales effort
nodes.notes: Scoped MECE split: for the next 90 days, does each of two disjoint client groups receive any sales effort above its start-of-period baseline? Existing means active paying clients on day one. New means all other prospective clients, including former clients. These definitions remain fixed for the period. Existing-only, new-only, both and neither exhaust the two yes/no allocation choices without overlap. Products, channels, absolute effort and the split within both are separate decisions. Commercial suitability remains unknown.

nodes.label: Existing clients only
nodes.notes: Additional sales effort goes to existing clients; new-client activity stays at its planned baseline. Proposed alternative, not a recommendation.

nodes.label: Current clients have unmet needs
nodes.notes: Tentative case: current clients have actionable unmet needs and delivery capacity is available. Counterpoint: familiar relationships do not prove budget or demand. Next test: review specific expansion opportunities and what would make each client act within 90 days. Compare the result against the agreed objective and effort limit.

nodes.label: New clients only
nodes.notes: Additional sales effort goes to the new-client group; existing-client sales activity stays at its planned baseline. A prospect who becomes a client during the period remains in the new group for this allocation analysis.

nodes.label: New-client demand is reachable
nodes.notes: Tentative case: a defined prospect group has a reachable, valuable problem and existing-client expansion is less promising for the objective. Counterpoint: acquisition may require more effort and take longer; neither is established here. Next test: inspect concrete prospect needs, access and buying timing before committing extra effort.

nodes.label: Both groups
nodes.notes: Both existing and new client groups receive additional sales effort. This includes any positive allocation to each group; it does not imply equal effort. The amount allocated to each is a later decision.

nodes.label: Capacity can cover both groups
nodes.notes: Tentative case: opportunities in each group justify attention and capacity can support both. Counterpoint: fragmented effort may weaken execution. Next test: compare a small opportunity sample from each group against the same objective and effort limit. The groups can compete for shared capacity; disjoint categories do not imply independent outcomes.

nodes.label: No additional sales effort
nodes.notes: Neither group receives extra sales effort. Already planned activity continues. This preserves a no-change alternative without equating it to stopping all sales.

nodes.label: The baseline plan is sufficient
nodes.notes: Tentative case: delivery commitments or another use of capacity have greater near-term value than extra sales work. Counterpoint: leaving the baseline unchanged may create a later pipeline gap. Next test: review committed workload and the consequences of keeping the current sales plan before treating this option as prudent or ruling it out.

uncertainties: The commercial objective and available extra effort are not yet specified.
Demand, buying timing and delivery capacity are unverified.
The allocation categories are complete within the stated scope; their relative value is unknown.
nextSteps: Define the 90-day objective and available extra effort.
Compare specific opportunities in both client groups against that objective.
Keep all four allocations open until the evidence supports a preference.

problem.situation: Extra sales effort could go to existing clients, new clients, both or neither over the next 90 days.
problem.desiredChange: The commercial objective still needs to be agreed.
problem.constraints: Available extra effort, demand and delivery capacity are not yet known.
